cards.title: Introduction to React Deployment
cards.content:
Deploying a React application involves compiling your source code into optimized, static assets (HTML, CSS, and JS) that can be served efficiently by web servers.

Unlike development where files are compiled on-the-fly, production deployment requires running a build process:

# For Vite-based React apps
npm run build

# For Create React App (CRA)
npm run build

This generates a dist/ or build/ directory containing minified and bundled files ready for production hosting.

cards.title: Order the steps to build and deploy a React application locally

items.text: Run 'npm install' to ensure all dependencies are resolved.
Execute 'npm run build' to generate the production-ready static assets.
Test the build locally using a static server tool like 'serve'.

cards.title: Environment Variables in Production
cards.content:
React applications run entirely in the user's browser, meaning your environment variables are embedded into the JS bundle during build-time.

Crucial Rule: Never store secret keys, passwords, or private credentials in React environment variables!

Prefix requirements based on your build tool:

  • Vite: Prefix variables with VITE_ (e.g., VITE_API_URL) and access via import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL.
  • Create React App: Prefix variables with REACT_APP_ (e.g., REACT_APP_API_URL) and access via process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL.

cards.title: The Single Page Application (SPA) Routing Challenge
cards.content:
When using client-side routing libraries like React Router, navigating to /dashboard works fine internally. However, if a user refreshes the page on /dashboard, the hosting server will look for a physical file named /dashboard/index.html, resulting in a 404 Not Found error.

To fix this, you must configure your hosting provider to redirect all requests to your main index.html file, allowing React Router to handle the URL resolution on the client side.

For example, Netlify uses a _redirects file containing:

/*    /index.html   200

cards.title: Why do React SPAs require custom redirect configurations on hosting servers?

options.text: Because client-side routes do not map to physical files on the server, causing server-side 404 errors on direct navigation or page refresh.
Because hosting servers cannot run JavaScript files unless a redirect configuration is provided.
Because React Router requires server-side authentication to load the index.html fallback file.
To speed up application loading times by bypassing the index.html page execution.

pairs.right: Free static hosting ideal for personal portfolios; requires configuring a homepage property in package.json.
Zero-configuration platform designed by creators of Next.js; features seamless preview deployments for pull requests.
Enterprise-grade static website hosting combined with a global CDN for low latency.
Popular static platform featuring simple drag-and-drop deployment and '_redirects' file support for SPAs.

cards.title: Automated Deployments with CI/CD
cards.content:
Manually building and dragging static files to a hosting platform is error-prone. Modern engineering teams use CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery) pipelines.

With GitHub Actions, Netlify, or Vercel integration, every push to your main branch can trigger an automated pipeline that:

  1. Lints your code for syntax issues.
  2. Runs your unit tests (e.g., using Vitest or Jest).
  3. Builds the static bundle.
  4. Deploys the assets directly to your hosting server.

cards.title: Order the stages of a standard React CI/CD GitHub Actions Workflow

items.text: Checkout the repository code onto a virtual runner.
Install dependencies using 'npm ci' to ensure clean, reproducible builds.
Run automated test suites with 'npm run test'.
Execute the production build process with environment variables configured.
Push the compiled directory (dist/build) to your chosen cloud hosting platform.
